title: Tipping With the Arm Out: The Centre of Mass of Base, Arm and Load, and How Hard the Base May Brake or Turn

questions.question: What moves when the arm moves?
options: The base's wheelbase and track
Only the load on the front wheels
The centre of mass of the whole, and so the tipping limits
The friction of the floor
questions.explanation: The arm's links and whatever it holds are part of the mass. Reaching 0.65 m forward moved the centre of the whole from -0.006 m to 0.069 m.

questions.question: The braking limit with the arm tucked was:
questions.explanation: Tucked, the centre is low and near the middle. Reaching it was 8.88, and with 5 kg in the hand 5.19; 5.89 is what the wheels grip on a dry floor.

questions.question: With 5 kg in the hand the braking limit was:
options: 8.88 m/s2, still above what the wheels grip
5.89 m/s2, set by the wheels
5.19 m/s2, below what the wheels would grip
11.01 m/s2, unchanged, since the load is at the hand
questions.explanation: The wheels would allow 5.89 m/s2 on a dry floor. With the load the base tips at 5.19, so tipping comes before skidding.

questions.question: What does a centred mass give?
options: A limit twice that of 19-09
No limit: a centred mass cannot tip
The same limit forward as sideways
The formula of 19-09: g times half the track over the height
questions.explanation: With no offset the general rule reduces to the simple one, which is how the test checks it.

questions.question: Why is a limit chosen for the tucked arm unsafe?
options: The wheels grip less when the arm is out
The loaded or extended arm has a lower limit
The tucked limit is for braking only
It is safe, as long as the floor is dry
questions.explanation: A braking limit of 11.01 m/s2 holds for the tucked arm. With 5 kg at full reach the base tips at 5.19, less than half.

questions.question: Which turn is the dangerous one?
options: Towards the side the arm is reaching to
Away from the side the arm is reaching to
Any turn at more than 4.22 m/s2
A turn while braking
questions.explanation: The arm out to one side moves the centre toward the wheels on that side, so there is less lever to hold the base down: 4.22 against 7.92 m/s2.
